tool_input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(audit): sweep Bash command and six sibling prose keys for PII

promptBearingKeys named twelve tool_input keys and not `command`, so an
address inside `bd update -d "..."` or `git config user.email` sealed
verbatim into a git-tracked audit chunk -- twice per line, in
tool_input.command and again in tool_input_preview. The inconsistency is
the defect: send_email's body was already reduced by this policy, so the
system stated a protection for address-shaped content and then missed it
on the tool carrying the most model-authored text of any on the surface.

Six further keys join it, each earned by a tool actually writing prose
under it rather than by the name sounding prose-like:

  old_string, new_string  Edit -- file content, and `content` was already
                          swept for Write: same bytes, same file, other key
  args                    Skill -- carries a whole /loop poll prompt
  title                   the github PR tools -- sibling of `body`, already
  commit_title            covered; a merge commit message is also where a
  commit_message          Co-Authored-By trailer address lands

Evidence, from a survey of this repo's 224 sealed chunks: `command` holds
5,293 of all tool_input keys, more than every other tool combined, and 26
address-shaped runs -- of which 15 are real addresses (jim@, claude@,
adb@, and noreply@anthropic.com from a commit heredoc, 9 times).
old_string, new_string, and args already hold real addresses too. The
remaining three keys were absent only because the leak had not landed yet.

Forward-looking by construction: chunks already sealed are not rewritten,
because a sealed chunk cannot be hand-edited without breaking its seal
(`ethos audit quarantine` is the path if one ever must be). Future chunks
are clean; existing ones are unchanged.

The widening is not free, and the cost is now measured rather than
assumed. emailPattern accepts two legitimate non-prose shell tokens:
git@github.com in a clone line, and a Go toolchain module path
(golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.26.5.linux-amd64), which satisfies the
lettered-TLD anchor at `.linux` where the shorter gopkg.in/yaml.v3@v3.0.1
does not. Both are now rewritten in the log. The pattern is deliberately
not narrowed to exempt them -- one pattern serves every key, so a
carve-out keeping a clone line legible would open the same hole in a mail
subject. Both shapes are pinned in TestEmailPattern_AddressShapedNonAddresses
so the redaction is a known property, not a future bug report; the
emailPattern doc comment, which claimed the TLD anchor kept module
versions out, is corrected to say which ones it does not.

Tests: 8 new table cases plus TestBuildAuditEntry_BashCommandPII, all
observed failing against pre-fix code, with the address present in both
tool_input.command and tool_input_preview in the failure output.
TestBuildAuditEntry_BashCommandNoAddressUnchanged pins the negative --
an ordinary shell line comes back byte-identical with the `redacted`
marker omitted entirely, so the other 5,267 commands do not churn.

Verified through the real entry point (`ethos hook audit-log`, the
command plugin/hooks/audit-log.sh runs) in a scratch repo: the pre-fix
binary on PATH writes `git config user.email adb@punt-labs.com`
unredacted with no marker; a post-fix build writes [redacted-email] in
both fields with redacted:true, leaves the ordinary line byte-identical,
and does not crash on a payload with no tool_input at all.

make check: 29 ok, 0 FAIL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

tool_input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# newchunks.sh — what address-shaped runs did the pre-commit seal just
# commit, from this session's own tool calls?
set -euo pipefail
repo=<repo>
pat='[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+[.][A-Za-z]{2,}'

git -C "$repo" show --name-only --format= deaf15f |
  grep 'audit-.*jsonl' |
  while read -r f; do
    git -C "$repo" show "deaf15f:$f"
  done |
  jq -r --arg pat "$pat" '
    select(.tool_input != null)
    | .tool as $t | .tool_input | to_entries[] | .key as $k
    | (.value | tostring) | [match($pat; "g").string] | unique[]
    | "\($t)\t\($k)\t\(.)"' |
  sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
